crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Invoice Capture and Coding
children.blurb: Invoice capture and coding covers the intake of supplier invoices from paper, PDF, email and electronic formats, the extraction of header and line item data, and the assignment of general ledger accounts, cost centres, tax codes and project or department dimensions.

children.name: Customer Credit Risk
children.blurb: Customer credit risk in payables and receivables covers the likelihood that a customer will fail to pay an invoice on time or in full.

children.name: Programmable Settlement and Escrow
children.blurb: Programmable settlement and escrow covers systems that hold funds or payment instructions and release them automatically when predefined conditions are met.

children.name: Collections and Payment Plans
children.blurb: Collections and payment plans in the AI Accountant covers the systems that manage overdue invoices, schedule customer payments, and decide when to escalate or offer revised terms.

children.name: Working Capital Timing
children.blurb: Working capital timing covers the deliberate scheduling of cash inflows from receivables and outflows to payables to shorten the cash conversion cycle.

sections.body: This field covers the money a business owes and the money it is owed. Artificial intelligence is now reading supplier invoices, matching them to purchase orders, and posting them to accounting systems. It is also scoring customers for credit risk, suggesting payment terms, and deciding when to release funds held in escrow. Collections work uses AI to choose which overdue accounts to contact, what message to send, and when to send it. Working capital models predict cash shortfalls and surpluses from invoice and payment data.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Invoice capture and coding is the most mature part, with high accuracy on standard invoices but weaker results on unusual layouts or handwritten notes. Customer credit risk models work well for businesses with long credit histories, but they struggle with new or thin-file customers and can inherit bias from old lending data. Programmable settlement and escrow is technically possible on blockchains and payment rails, yet adoption is limited by legal uncertainty and integration cost. Collections and payment plans can automate reminders and simple negotiations, but difficult cases still need human judgment. Working capital timing gives useful forecasts, but it cannot remove the basic uncertainty of when a customer will actually pay.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader who wants to see how invoices enter the system should start with Invoice Capture and Coding. From there, Customer Credit Risk explains how the system decides whether to extend credit before payment is due. Programmable Settlement and Escrow covers the mechanics of releasing money when conditions are met, which connects to Collections and Payment Plans for what happens when payment does not arrive. Working Capital Timing pulls the other pages together by showing how all these decisions affect cash on hand over time.
